fact: Two types of graphics can be represented: vector graphics and bitmap graphics
Any graphic is made up from a series of pixels, that is picture elements, and each pixel is an individual point on the screen
In the bitmap illustration only black and white are assumed, so each pixel is stored as a single 1 or 0
The quality of a bitmap image depends on the number of pixels: more pixels means higher resolution and a clearer image
In the storage worked example the image is 4 inches by 6 inches at a resolution of 300 dots per linear inch and is black and white
The length is 6 times 300, which is 1800 pixels, and the breadth is 4 times 300, which is 1200 pixels, so the total is 1800 times 1200, that is 2,160,000 pixels
Black and white means 1 bit per pixel, so the storage is 2,160,000 bits, which is 270,000 bytes, that is 263.4 KBytes
In vector graphics each image is made from objects such as a line, a rectangle or a circle, and every object has attributes which define it
To draw a rectangle in vector graphics we need the start X and Y coordinates, the length, the breadth, the thickness and colour of the lines, the type of line such as dashed, and the fill colour

Advantages of vector graphics, the draw packages, are that images can be enlarged without losing resolution, objects can be edited by changing their attributes, objects can be layered on top or behind, and images take up less disc space
Vector graphics are ideal for drawing plans, using a library of objects
Advantages of bit-mapped graphics, the paint packages, are that each pixel can be altered and that they are more realistic when used for photos or real life
